nodes.content: Design an incremental compiler that soundly reuses cross-module typechecking results despite edits changing overload and trait resolution.
requirements: Match clean-build diagnostics and executable behavior across edits, including newly applicable candidates and ambiguities.
Reuse at least 95% of typechecking results for declarations whose resolution dependencies remain semantically unchanged.

nodes.content: Cache typechecks with referenced-interface fingerprints and scoped candidate-set guards; invalidate on applicability, ranking, ambiguity, or selected-implementation changes.
How can candidate-set guards detect newly applicable imported trait implementations without invalidating unrelated declarations?
Scoped trait/receiver-head indexes with blanket-impl wildcard buckets detect additions; recheck affected queries, invalidating only changed resolution outcomes.
Record scoped overload/trait queries and wildcard buckets; replay affected queries after edits, invalidate changed outcomes, retain semantically unchanged typechecks.
Implement ResolverCache v1 query logging, wildcard buckets, and post-edit replay; benchmark 1,000 cross-module edits for clean-build parity and reuse.
ResolverCache v1 patch adds scoped query logs, wildcard buckets, outcome-sensitive replay, and a 1,000-edit clean-build comparison harness.
Run ResolverCache v1's 1,000-edit harness across imported blanket impls and overload ambiguities; check clean-build parity and ≥95% unchanged-declaration reuse.
Across 1,000 edits including imported blanket impls, replay caught all new candidates; diagnostic/executable parity was 100%, unchanged-declaration reuse 97.2%.
Use ResolverCache v1 to test 500 same-head generic-bound edits and scoped re-exports against clean builds, tracking missed candidates and reuse.
Across 500 same-head bound edits and scoped re-exports, seven bound relaxations escaped replay, causing seven clean-build diagnostic mismatches.
Which additional query dependencies catch same-head bound relaxations and scoped re-exports without sacrificing unchanged-declaration reuse?
Fingerprint semantic constraints of every head-matched candidate and scoped import reachability; replay affected queries, retaining unchanged typechecks.
Extend ResolverCache with head-matched constraint fingerprints and per-scope visibility fingerprints; replay affected queries and measure clean-build parity and reuse.
Add constraint/visibility fingerprints to ResolverCache v2; rerun 500 targeted and 1,000 baseline edits for parity and ≥95% reuse.
ResolverCache v2 eliminated all seven misses: 0/1,500 clean-build diagnostic/executable mismatches; unchanged-declaration reuse was 96.1% targeted, 96.8% baseline.
Run ResolverCache v2 through v1's harness on 300 multi-hop re-export and bound-strengthening edits; verify clean-build parity and reuse.
Among 300 edits, four multi-hop re-exports bypassed scope fingerprints, producing four clean-build ambiguity mismatches despite 96.4% reuse.
Fingerprint transitive, cycle-safe export reachability per lookup scope and namespace alongside candidate constraints; replay queries when either digest changes.
Combine SCC-aware scope/namespace reachability digests with constraint fingerprints; test 1,800 edits and cyclic re-exports for parity and ≥95% reuse.
Implement ResolverCache v3 with SCC-aware reachability digests; rerun 1,800 prior edits plus cyclic re-exports for parity and ≥95% reuse.
ResolverCache v3 recorded 0/2,000 clean-build diagnostic/executable mismatches across prior and cyclic edits; unchanged-declaration reuse reached 95.7%.
Use differential Datalog for scoped candidate sets and constraint proofs; invalidate only declarations whose semantic typechecking inputs change.
Can differential Datalog track negative candidate facts and trait-proof changes across module visibility edits without excessive recomputation?
Stratified differential relations for visibility, candidate applicability, and proof absence propagate edits while preserving ≥95% unchanged-declaration reuse.
Prototype stratified differential Datalog; replay ResolverCache v3’s 2,000 edits, measuring clean-build parity, unchanged-declaration reuse, and recomputed proofs.
Differential Datalog had 0/2,000 clean-build diagnostic/executable mismatches, reused 96.2% of unchanged declarations, and recomputed 8.4% of trait proofs.
Use per-declaration resolution certificates covering winners, rejected alternatives, and ambiguities; revalidate against versioned scoped candidate indexes.
Implement certificate capture and index-delta revalidation; compare 2,000 cross-module edits against clean builds for diagnostic/executable parity and ≥95% reuse.
Implement CertCache v1 with rejected-candidate witnesses and scoped index-delta checks; replay 2,000 edits against clean-build diagnostics and executables.
CertCache v1 patch stores resolution certificates and candidate-index deltas, with a 2,000-edit clean-build comparison runner.
Run CertCache v1’s 2,000-edit runner, including newly applicable impls and ambiguities; measure clean-build parity and unchanged-declaration reuse.
CertCache v1 missed five same-head bound relaxations absent index deltas, yielding five clean-build ambiguity mismatches despite 97.1% reuse.
Stress-test CertCache v1 on 400 cyclic re-export and blanket-impl edits; compare candidate certificates, diagnostics, executables, and reuse against clean builds.
On 400 cyclic-re-export and blanket-impl edits, CertCache v1 caught newly visible candidates: zero diagnostic/executable mismatches, 96.6% unchanged-declaration reuse.
How can certificates detect same-head bound relaxations when candidate-index membership stays unchanged without invalidating unrelated declarations?
Versioned constraint fingerprints for every head-matched candidate trigger certificate revalidation on bound changes, preserving unrelated typechecks.
Add head-matched constraint fingerprints to CertCache v2; rerun 2,400 prior edits for parity and ≥95% unchanged-declaration reuse.
CertCache v2 caught all five bound relaxations: 0/2,400 clean-build diagnostic/executable mismatches and 96.3% unchanged-declaration reuse.
Rebuild global candidate indexes after edits; replay cached lookups against fresh indexes, reusing declarations with identical typed-resolution outcomes.
How can lookup replay detect changed inferred receiver or expected types without rechecking every cached declaration?
Fingerprint upstream type inputs and inferred lookup contexts; propagate changed fingerprints before replay, leaving declarations with stable inputs cached.
Build ContextReplay v1 with upstream-type fingerprints and fresh candidate indexes; compare clean-build parity and unchanged-declaration reuse on 2,000 edits.
Implement ContextReplay v1; run 2,000 edits including inferred-receiver shifts, comparing diagnostics, executables, and unchanged-declaration reuse with clean builds.
ContextReplay v1 caught all 61 inferred-receiver shifts with zero parity mismatches; global-index churn reduced unchanged-declaration reuse to 92.8%.
Cache declaration constraint templates separately from resolution outcomes; reinstantiate only sites affected by edited signatures, imports, or inferred types.
Implement template/outcome separation, track lookup-context inputs and candidate visibility, then differential-test 2,000 edits for parity and ≥95% reuse.
Implement TemplateCache v1 with constraint templates and lookup-context dependencies; replay 2,000 cross-module edits against clean-build diagnostics and executables.
TemplateCache v1 patch separates cached constraint templates from resolution outcomes and logs inferred-context and candidate-visibility dependencies.
Run TemplateCache v1 on 2,000 edits covering candidate additions, inferred-context shifts, and ambiguity; measure parity and unchanged-declaration reuse.
TemplateCache v1 matched clean-build diagnostics/executables on all 2,000 edits and reused 95.4% of unchanged-declaration typechecks.
Adopt CertCache v2 as the base, adding SCC-aware visibility and inferred-context guards; validate combined parity and ≥95% reuse.
